Decaying Risk Algorithm

How SAFE BITE computes the overall product risk score from individual additive ratings.

The Mathematical Model

Rather than taking a simple average, which dilutes the impact of high-toxicity additives, SAFE BITE uses a Decaying-Contribution Model. This algorithm ensures that the highest risk additive dictates the baseline, and additional additives contribute diminishing risk increments.

{"$$Score_{raw} = S_1 + \\sum_{i=2}^{N} \\left( S_i \\times 0.5^{i-1} \\right)$$"}

{"Where $S$ represents individual additive risk scores sorted descending ($S_1 \\ge S_2 \\ge \\dots \\ge S_N$)."}

Step-by-Step Calculation

1

Collect & Sort Risk Scores

Gather all detected additives and query their base risk scores ($0–100$) from SQLite. Sort them in descending order.

2

Establish Primary Score

The highest score ($S_1$) serves as the primary base. For instance, if scores are $[70, 45, 30, 5]$, the primary base is 70.

3

Apply Diminishing Weights

For each subsequent additive, halve its contribution coefficient:

  • 2nd Additive: $Score \times 0.5$ (e.g. $45 \times 0.5 = 22.5$)
  • 3rd Additive: $Score \times 0.25$ (e.g. $30 \times 0.25 = 7.5$)
  • 4th Additive: $Score \times 0.125$ (e.g. $5 \times 0.125 = 0.625$)

Raw score sum: $70 + 22.5 + 7.5 + 0.625 = 100.625$

4

Additive Count Bonus

To account for cumulative ingestion complexity, a flat threshold-based bonus is added:

Additives Count Bonus Score
> 3 additives +8 points
> 5 additives +15 points
> 8 additives +20 points
5

High Risk Safeguard Rule

If the database flags ANY detected additive as High Risk (high_risk_flag = 1), the final calculated risk score will never fall below 65 (ensuring it stays classified as "High Risk" overall).

6

Clamp & Classify

The score is rounded to the nearest integer and clamped to a maximum of 100.

0–30: Low Risk 31–60: Moderate Risk 61–100: High Risk
